name: Missing npm package
root_cause: The code imports a package that is not listed in package.json, so it is not installed on the build server.
fix_steps: Install the package: `npm install {module}`
Commit both package.json and package-lock.json
Redeploy

name: Wrong import path
root_cause: A relative import points to a file that does not exist, usually a typo or wrong letter case (Linux build servers are case-sensitive).
fix_steps: Open the file that imports `{path}` and correct the path to the real file
Check the letter case of folder and file names
Run `npm run build` locally, then redeploy

name: TypeScript type error
root_cause: The TypeScript compiler found a value whose type does not match what the code declares, so the production build stops.
fix_steps: Open the file and line shown in the error
Change the value or the declared type so they match
Run `npx tsc --noEmit` locally until it passes, then redeploy

name: Syntax error
regex: (?:SyntaxError|error TS1005|error TS1128|error TS1109|Unexpected token|Unterminated string|'\}' expected)
root_cause: The code cannot be parsed: a bracket, quote or comma is missing or extra.
fix_steps: Open the file and line in the error and look for a missing `}`, `)` or quote just before it
Format the file with your editor to spot the mismatch
Run the build locally, then redeploy

name: Missing environment variable
regex: (?:\b(?P<var>[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{2,})\b (?:is not defined|is not set|is required|is missing)|Missing (?:required )?(?:environment|env) variable)
root_cause: The app needs a secret or setting from the environment that is not configured on the server. It works locally because it is in your local .env file.
fix_steps: Add `{var}` in your hosting dashboard (e.g. Vercel/Render → Settings → Environment Variables) for the right environment
Never commit the value to git
Redeploy so the new variable is picked up

name: Node.js version mismatch
root_cause: The build server runs a different Node.js version than the project or one of its packages requires.
fix_steps: Set the Node version in the hosting settings (or `engines.node` in package.json) to the required major version
Match it locally with `nvm use`
Redeploy

name: Dependency version conflict
regex: (?:npm ERR! code ERESOLVE|ERESOLVE unable to resolve dependency tree|ERESOLVE could not resolve)
root_cause: Two packages need incompatible versions of the same peer dependency, so npm refuses to install.
fix_steps: Read the 'Found' and 'Could not resolve' lines to see which package conflicts
Upgrade or downgrade one of them to compatible versions
As a temporary workaround only: `npm install --legacy-peer-deps` and commit the lock file

name: Port already in use
root_cause: Another process is already listening on the port the app tries to use, or the app ignores the PORT the platform assigns.
fix_steps: Find and stop the process using port {port} (`lsof -i :{port}` or `netstat -ano | findstr {port}`)
Make the app listen on `process.env.PORT` instead of a hard-coded port
Restart the service

name: Database connection refused
root_cause: The app cannot reach its database: the database is down, the host/port is wrong for this environment, or a firewall blocks it.
fix_steps: Check the database is running and reachable from the server at {host}:{port}
Make sure the production DATABASE_URL points to the production host, not localhost
Allow the server's IP in the database firewall / network rules, then restart

name: Kubernetes CrashLoopBackOff
root_cause: The container starts and exits immediately, so Kubernetes keeps restarting it. The real error is in the previous container's logs.
fix_steps: Read the crash reason: `kubectl logs <pod> --previous` and `kubectl describe pod <pod>`
Check the start command, required environment variables and config maps
Fix the cause, then `kubectl rollout restart deployment/<name>`

name: Image pull failed
regex: (?:ImagePullBackOff|ErrImagePull|pull access denied|manifest unknown|repository does not exist)
root_cause: The cluster cannot download the container image: the name or tag is wrong, or the registry needs credentials the cluster does not have.
fix_steps: Check the image name and tag exist in the registry (`docker pull <image>`)
If the registry is private, create an imagePullSecret and reference it in the deployment
Update the deployment and watch `kubectl get pods -w`

name: Out of memory (OOMKilled)
regex: (?:OOMKilled|[Ee]xit [Cc]ode:?\s*137|JavaScript heap out of memory|Out of memory: Killed process)
root_cause: The process used more memory than its limit, so the system killed it (exit code 137).
fix_steps: Raise the memory limit (e.g. `resources.limits.memory` in Kubernetes, or the instance size)
For Node builds, set `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096`
Check for memory leaks or very large in-memory data if it keeps happening

name: Docker COPY failed
regex: (?:COPY failed|failed to compute cache key[^\n]*not found|"/(?P<path>[^"]+)": not found)
root_cause: The Dockerfile copies a file that is not in the build context: wrong path, wrong build directory, or excluded by .dockerignore.
fix_steps: Check that `{path}` exists relative to the folder you run `docker build` from
Check .dockerignore is not excluding it
Fix the COPY path or the build context and rebuild
